text:
alex: Hey team — after last night's CMK rotation I'm seeing intermittent AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt for the ingestion service role. Started ~00:30 UTC. Example error from the pod logs:
```
ERROR: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111111111:assumed-role/ingest-role/ingest-session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111111:key/abcd-ef01-2345 (Service: AWSKMS; Status Code: 400; Error Code: AccessDeniedException)
```
Anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking_face:
messages_ordered: kms-rotator-bot: Automated rotation: alias/aws/redwood-ingest -> key/abcd-ef01-2345 completed at 2026-03-19T00:12:10Z :rotating_light:
alex: Confirmed the alias now points to the new key id. S3 objects encrypted under the alias should decrypt transparently, but our ingest pipeline shows failures for some objects.
maria: Can you paste the role ARN + whether the service assumes role with session tags or session policy? Also did we change any permission boundaries recently?
alex: Role: arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/ingest-role. We do assume-role from the ingestion ECS task with tags (team=ingest, env=prod). No intentional boundary change I know of but will check.

jin: A couple quick checks: 1) Verify alias -> key mapping (aws kms list-aliases); 2) Check CloudTrail for KMS:Decrypt Deny events (makes it easier to see which policy denied); 3) check for grant tokens if rotation used grants.
trent: Also remember permission boundaries and session policies can silently remove kms:Decrypt even if the role's identity policy allows it. The boundary could have been updated via infra rollout.

maria: Two likely failure modes: 1) Key policy requires a principal tag or specific aws:PrincipalTag and your assume-role call didn't pass the expected tag (session tags must be forwarded). 2) A permissions boundary or session policy removed kms:Decrypt. Can you show the role's permissions boundary and the assume-role command?

alex: We use the standard assume via the task role provider; the upstream assume-role call looks like: `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/ingest-role --role-session-name ingest-session --serial-number arn:aws:iam::111111111:mfa/user --token-code 123456 --duration-seconds 3600 --tags Key=team,Value=ingest Key=env,Value=prod`. I verified tags are present in the STS response.

jin: If tags were present in the STS response but the key policy checks aws:PrincipalTag at KMS evaluation time, note KMS uses session tags only if they are passed on the assume-role call and if the principal that attempts decrypt is the assumed role session. Also check for an IAM policy Condition like "StringEquals": {"aws:PrincipalTag/team": "security"} which would deny non-matching tags.

trent: Another angle — because we rotated the key, some code paths may still be using Grant tokens from pre-rotation grants. If decrypts are using a grant token that references the old key, you'll see odd denies. Search CloudTrail for `GrantToken` in the KMS API calls.

alex: I checked the permission boundary on the role: we do have a boundary arn:aws:iam::111111111:policy/infra-boundary-prod. It contains a block that looks like: "Action": ["kms:*"], "Effect": "Deny", "Resource": "*", "Condition": {"StringNotEquals": {"aws:PrincipalTag/env":"prod"}} — which is intended to deny KMS ops unless env=prod. Weirdly our session tags are present but the boundary might be evaluated before session tags are applied?

maria: Permission boundaries are evaluated during IAM policy evaluation and can interact with session tags. If the boundary denies KMS unless a tag exists, and something in the assume flow strips tags (e.g., an intermediate role or federation step), you'll hit deny. Could be an OIDC provider or task role token exchange that doesn't forward tags.

jin: Quick repro: run `aws sts get-caller-identity` from the pod and `aws iam get-role --role-name ingest-role` from an admin shell, then from the pod run `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob --key-id alias/redwood-ingest` and capture the error. Also grep for `sessionTags` in the CloudTrail assume-role event.

alex: Ran `get-caller-identity` inside pod, shows assumed-role arn:aws:sts::111111111:assumed-role/ingest-role/ingest-session and STS assume-role event in CT includes the sessionTags. But decrypt still 403. I dug deeper and found an infra rollout earlier today that updated the permission boundary to require `aws:PrincipalTag/team = security` for all kms:Decrypt — that was my mistake in the rollout. Our ingestion role has team=ingest, so boundary denied kms:Decrypt even though role policy allowed it. The rotation just changed which code path hits KMS and surfaced it.
trent: Nice catch. So root cause = overly strict permission boundary combined with key rotation surfacing path differences. Remediation?

alex: We reverted the boundary change (rolled back infra PR) and kicked the tasks. Decrypt errors stopped. For long-term: 1) update boundary to allow service roles with proper tag sets or use resource-based key policy principals instead of boundary deny, 2) add CloudTrail-based alerting for KMS AccessDenied spikes post-rotation, 3) test rotations in a staging alias with grant tokens. I'll open a follow-up runbook PR.
maria: Recommend also adding a small smoke test in the rotation job that runs a decrypt with the role's credentials to catch this before full cutover. :white_check_mark:
